title: AI Hallucinations in State Farm Insurance Outside Lawyers' Filings

reading.body:
This is a model hallucination failure occurring at the output-use stage of a legal workflow. A generative AI tool named Irys produced fictitious case citations, nonexistent case titles, and fabricated quotes, and those outputs were incorporated into at least eight court filings without being caught before submission. The failure mode is a model asserting invented legal authority as fact, a well-documented pattern with generative AI systems applied to legal research.

The failure reached the court because no human verification step confirmed that cited cases actually exist before the filings were submitted. Checking whether a cited case exists in a legal database is a routine task, and the hallucinations would have been caught at that step. The lead trial counsel accepted responsibility and the firm stated it updated its AI policies after the problem was identified.

What is not established is whether the court has imposed any sanctions, whether the false citations affected any rulings, or what the outcome of the underlying dispute will be, as the trial had not yet taken place at the time of reporting.

reports.title: State Farm defense lawyers admit AI generated fake cases in LA lawsuit
AI hallucinated case law in insurance company’s filings in L.A. County house fire dispute
AI Hallucinations in State Farm Insurance Outside Lawyers' Filings

summary:
# Summary

Lawyers representing State Farm in a Los Angeles lawsuit have admitted to using artificial intelligence that generated fake legal cases, nonexistent quotes, and false case holdings in court filings. The homeowner suing State Farm is Fa'alagilagi Meni-Siliga, whose home in Carson caught fire in 2020, became uninhabitable, and was never properly repaired despite contractor work. After delays in getting State Farm's approval for repairs and subsequent water damage from a storm, Meni-Siliga and her husband depleted their savings, declared bankruptcy, and lost their home to foreclosure. The case is scheduled for trial in October.

State Farm lawyer Jacquelene Robinson acknowledged using an AI tool called Irys that generated at least seven fake case citations across eight filings, along with incorrect case titles and quotes. Kenneth Katel, the lead trial counsel, apologized to the court and accepted responsibility for the filings while noting the firm has updated its AI policies. The broader legal industry increasingly uses generative AI, with a database tracking 1,922 documented legal hallucinations worldwide, mostly in the United States. Last year, a California attorney faced a record ten thousand dollar fine for using ChatGPT that produced 21 fabricated quotes.
